claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 7,000 infantry and 1,000 cavalry; side B (Spanish) 1,500 line troops, 6,500 recruits and 12,000 armed inhabitants, total 20,000.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. Not an opening muster; components are not added twice. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "side A (French) 7,000 infantry and 1,000 cavalry; side B (Spanish) 1,500 line troops, 6,500 recruits and 12,000 armed inhabitants, total 20,000."

claims.value: Napoleon’s mid-July note assigns side A 8,000 to Moncey while acknowledging no news of the Valencia expedition.
claims.rationale: Dated superior estimate after the assault, not proof of the assaulting or surviving population. English rendering (ours): "There is no news of the Valencia expedition, and General Moncey has 8,000 men."

claims.value: Toreno records Saint-March sharing arrangements to contain Moncey, and Conquista as captain-general addressed in the surrender demand; Caro’s printed Bodart attribution remains unreconciled.
claims.rationale: Caro’s identity is carried by the preceding paragraph retained on the page. Political and military authority are not reduced to one continuously effective commander. English rendering (ours): "On arrival he joined Saint-March and together they arranged how to contain the French marshal; at night Moncey sent the captain-general Count of Conquista a letter demanding surrender."

claims.value: Moncey ordered his battalions and assaulted the Cuarte gate and Santa Catalina battery.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Holding most of the Cuarte suburb, Moncey arrayed his battalions behind San Sebastian; they directed guns against Cuarte gate and Santa Catalina, attacked three times and were repulsed."

citations.locator: toreno-t1, printed p. 358, Internet Archive leaf 371; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Como Moncey era dueño de casi todo el arrabal de Cuarte, le fue fácil ordenar sus batallones detras del convento de San Sebastian. A su abrigo dirigieron los enemigos sus cañones contra la puerta de Cuarte y batería de Santa Catalina. Tres veces atacaron con el mayor ímpetu del lado de la primera, y otras tantas fueron rechazados.

claims.value: Side B used masonry walls and hastily built gate batteries and barricades.
claims.rationale: Permanent walls are inherited; the construction authority and phase of the separate temporary batteries remain unresolved. English rendering (ours): "Surrounded by an old masonry wall and a poor citadel; within sixty hours earth-filled sack batteries were built at the gates."
